Protocols / Phenotyping & imaging

Measuring cluster size

Phenotyping & imagingBy Various authorsVersion 1 · updated 2026-10-07

Imaging cluster cross-sectional area after 5 days of settling selection, for size segmentation.

Download (.docx) PDF

Adapted from the lab compendium Snowflake Yeast Protocols — Ratcliff Lab / MuLTEE (V2).

  1. Revive frozen stock, re-acclimate, and put through settling selection for 5 days (Culturing & settling selection › Daily growth and settling selection and Freezer stocks › Reviving strains from frozen stock).
  2. After the fifth day’s 24 h growth, pipette a random 1 mL subsample into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
  3. Add 0.5 mL sterile water to each well of a 12-well plate.
  4. Vortex the yeast sample gently and dilute into the water:
    1. Microscopic populations: 1,000-fold dilution.
    2. Macroscopic populations: 100-fold dilution.
  5. Shake the well plate gently to disperse clusters evenly across the well bottom.
  6. Image each well with a ×4 objective, capturing cluster cross-sectional area without disrupting 3D structure. Include a physical 100 μm scale bar per image for pixel-to-micrometer conversion.

Image analysis pipeline (cluster segmentation): zipped folder containing pipeline is attached — segments whole clusters (brightfield-based, supports single field-of-view and stitched whole-well images).
